name: Nahor
overview: Nahor was a male descendant in the early biblical genealogy, uniquely identified as the son of Serug. The Scriptures provide limited detail about his life beyond his lineage, highlighting his place within the patriarchal line. No specific tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Nahor means "the mound of Nahuru," a proper name not given by God. This meaning is preserved in the Hebrew text and serves primarily as an identifier rather than conveying a theological title.
familyAndRelationships: Nahor is explicitly recorded as the father of Terah and is inferred to be the son of Serug. These relationships place him within the ancestral line leading to Abraham, establishing his role in the biblical genealogy.
scriptureSignificance: Nahor holds significance as a key link in the genealogy from Serug to Terah, situating him in the ancestral line preceding Abraham. His family remained in Mesopotamia, and through his descendants, such as Bethuel and Laban, he contributed to the lineage of Rebekah and Rachel, who became wives within Abraham's family line. This connection preserved important family ties and maintained separation from Canaanite influences, underscoring God's providential care in the unfolding of His covenant promises.
